memo: Member: SYN-MCD-0003 (45 y/o, warehouse worker). Notice: Six-month renewal, respond by 2026-08-12 (25 days remaining). Screening: 72 hours/month (64h employment + 8h community service) = 8 hours SHORT of 80-hour standard. Both documents on hand and accepted (pay stubs for employment, signed volunteer log for community service). Exemptions checked: none apparent from case file (no mention of caregiver status, disability benefits, medical frailty, recent incarceration, or age 65+). Path forward: member must close 8-hour gap or claim/prove an exemption. Options: (1) Add 8+ more hours of any qualifying activity (work, school, job training, or community service) in the renewal month; (2) Confirm caretaker status (child ≤13 or disabled dependent) with birth certificate or care documentation; (3) Verify disability benefits (SSI/SSDI award letter) or medically frail status (provider letter). Strong deadline compliance: 26 days remain. All supporting documents for current activities are in place and meet standard. No barriers flagged.
member_impact:
Good news: your work and volunteer hours are documented and accepted. You're 8 hours short of the 80-hour requirement this month. Here's what you can do right away:

**Close the gap in the next 3 weeks:**
• Ask your warehouse employer for 8 extra hours of work, or
• Add 8 more hours at the food pantry or another qualifying volunteer position, or
• Start a job-training or school program for 8+ hours, or
• Tell us if you're caring for a child age 13 or younger, or a disabled family member — that might exempt you entirely.

**You have until August 12, 2026 to respond.** That's 25 days from today.

**What to gather now:**
• Your current pay stubs (you have these)
• Your volunteer log signed by the food pantry (you have this)
• If you add more hours: new pay stubs, volunteer log, or training records
• If you're a caregiver: child's birth certificate, benefits letter, or care paperwork

We're here to help. Bring everything you gather to your next visit, and we'll make sure it's submitted in time.
recommended_actions: Confirm whether member is caretaker of dependent child (≤13) or person with disability — if so, gather proof document (birth certificate, benefits record, or care documentation) per EX-CARETAKER
Ask member's employer for 8+ additional work hours during the renewal period, or request written confirmation of reduced schedule so hours can be credited prospectively
Explore expansion of food pantry volunteering or other qualifying community service for 8+ hours per month

Schedule follow-up visit 3–5 days before the 2026-08-12 deadline to review all documents and finalize submission

citations.quote: Adults age 19 to 64 covered through Medicaid expansion must complete at least 80 hours per month of qualifying activities, unless an exemption applies.

Qualifying activities include working for pay (including self-employment), attending school or an education program at least half-time, participating in a job-training or workforce program, and performing community service or volunteering with a qualifying organization. Hours from different activities may be combined freely.
Community service is proven with a volunteer log signed by the organization or a letter from it stating dates and hours.
If an exemption applies, the 80-hour requirement does not apply to you at all, and reporting hours is unnecessary. Always check exemptions before counting hours.

A parent, guardian, or caretaker relative of a dependent child age 13 or younger is exempt, as is a caretaker of a person with a disability. Proof is simple: the child's birth certificate, a benefits record showing the child's age, or documentation of the care relationship.
People receiving SSI or SSDI disability benefits are exempt, as are people age 65 and older (who generally qualify through other pathways) and former foster youth under age 26.

People who are medically frail are exempt, including those with disabling mental health or substance-use conditions, serious or complex medical conditions, and people receiving treatment in a substance-use disorder program.
